name: User agent string
plain: The text the browser sends naming its browser, version and operating system.
meaning: Says which browser, version and OS the person uses. Chrome has been reducing detail since 2022, but the string still gates features, and LinkedIn's extension probe only runs when it contains Chrome.

story.what_it_is: The text your browser sends naming its browser, version and operating system.

marketing.name: User-Agent reduction
marketing.pitch: Chrome has been trimming the string to give out less detail and moving the rest to client hints.

story.for_you: You never see it, but your browser sends it with every request. It is why a site knows you are on Safari on an iPhone and shows the right version of the page.
story.for_makers: It is the oldest way to tell browsers apart and still decides which code and features a site sends. Bot defence and analytics use it, even though it is easy to fake. Chrome now gives less detail than it once did.

use_cases.example: A site sends an older script file to an old browser it recognises from the string.
A browser game portal shows a note that a browser cannot run WebGL games well.
A streaming site picks a player that works in the visitor's browser.
A bot defence service blocks clients whose strings name known scraping tools.
A dashboard counts visits by browser and version.
An ad platform checks strings to filter out crawlers and fake traffic.
A professional network reads the string and extension clues to catch tools that scrape profiles.

technical_bounds: Can be changed by users and extensions
